subject: Urgent: scope for incident-time data handling during P0 throughput spike
messages:
From: Aisha Salah <aisha.salah@finovatecorp.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: ops@finovatecorp.com
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High error-rate + throughput spike — data retention questions

Jordan —

We saw a P0-like surge this morning between 08:40 and 09:05 PST: token-level error rates climbed to ~6% and latency P95 jumped above 1.8s for a few minutes. Our engineering lead (cc'd) asked for:

- a snapshot of request/response traces for the 08:40–09:05 window (per-route)
- any server-side logs that show batching behavior and fallback model routing events
- confirmation of how long request payloads (and partial responses) are retained in your systems — we need this for an internal incident review and compliance with our retention policy

We appreciate your help and need these artifacts by EOD today if possible. Also: please confirm whether any customer-provided PII was present in logs captured during the spike.

Thanks,
Aisha Salah
Head of Platform Ops
Finovate Corp

Attachments: spike_timeseries.csv (CSV), incident-annotated.png (image)
From: jordan.blake@redwood.com <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Salah <aisha.salah@finovatecorp.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ops@finovatecorp.com
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error-rate + throughput spike — data retention questions

Aisha —

Thanks for the heads up and apologies for the disruption. We're already triaging. Quick answers up front:

1) We will generate time-bounded runtime traces for 08:40–09:05 (segmented by route/model) and provide a zip.
2) Logs we can provide immediately: request metadata, batching decisions, model-fallback events, and runtime error stacks. Full token-level transcripts are stored only when you enable "full-logging"; by default we keep request headers and token hashes for 30 days.
3) Regarding PII: we do not persist raw customer responses in telemetry by default; any snippets present in traces are redacted using our content-redaction pipeline, but we will run an expedited scan and flag anything that looks like PII.

I'll loop in Karthik and Soojin for the evidence package and timeline. Marissa, can you help with exec-facing comms and confirm whether Finovate has an active evidence-access SLA in the portal?

Jordan Blake
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Aisha Salah <aisha.salah@finovatecorp.com>, ops@finovatecorp.com
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error-rate + throughput spike — data retention questions

Folks —

Triage notes from infra: between 08:38 and 08:56 we observed an unusual request fan-in on the route /v1/generate-chat that caused backpressure on the batcher. The runtime performed three automatic fallbacks to a smaller-quantized model to preserve latency SLOs; those fallbacks are logged as an array of events (see runtime_trace_segment-20270504.log).

Immediate plan for evidence:
- Package A: runtime_trace_segment-20270504.log (batching events, model routing, error stacks)
- Package B: request-level metadata CSV (no raw responses unless Finovate confirms they want full transcripts — redaction required)
- Package C: short executive timeline (one-pager) with impact metrics and mitigations

Privacy note: the runtime preserves request payloads for up to 72 hours in hot storage for troubleshooting; after that we keep hashed tokens for 30 days (configurable per-account). We can export the hot-storage snapshot for your legal/ops team under an access-controlled transfer and place a temporary legal hold if you request it.

Karthik
VP, Platform Engineering
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Salah <aisha.salah@finovatecorp.com>, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error-rate + throughput spike — data retention questions

Aisha —

We're assembling the packages. A few decisions we need from you to scope the delivery: 

1) Do you want full request/response transcripts (we will run redaction, but this increases delivery time and requires an approved transfer agreement)? Reply YES/NO.
2) Do you want us to include application-level headers (session IDs, customer request IDs) in Package B? These speed triage but are considered sensitive.
3) Would Finovate like an S3-accessed evidence bundle (temporary pre-signed link) or a secure SFTP transfer to your ops bucket?

If we hear back within 2 hours we'll aim to deliver the initial evidence bundle (A+B) by 16:00 PST. If you need legal hold, mention it explicitly and include the retention window you require.

—Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Aisha Salah <aisha.salah@finovatecorp.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, Samir Rao <samir.rao@finovatecorp.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error-rate + throughput spike — data retention questions

Thanks — quick answers: 

1) NO to full transcripts for now. Please include hashed tokens and any request IDs.
2) YES to application-level headers (session ID and request ID).
3) S3 pre-signed link is fine; our security team will fetch it.

Also please initiate a 7-day legal hold on hot-storage artifacts for the 08:38–09:05 window (we'll follow up with our counsel on language). We need an exec summary for our CTO and a short list of mitigations for next week (can be bullet points).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Aisha
